department: Biochemistry, Cell and Molecular Biology (College of Science and Engineering / College of Medicine)

deadline.value: Fall admission deadline is January 10, 2027 (late consideration only if matched with a mentor who requests an exception; admission offers sent by March 15, decision due April 15).
deadline.quote: Complete applications received by January 10 will be considered for admission into the program the following fall semester.

gre_general.value: GRE, MCAT, or similar test scores are optional (institution code 1106, department code 0203).
gre_general.quote: Optional: GRE, MCAT, or other similar test scores may be submitted.

gre_subject.value: ETS discontinued the GRE Biology Subject Test in May 2021 (Subject Tests remain only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact prospective faculty advisors before applying and match with a faculty advisor willing to host them in their lab to be considered for admission.
supervisor.quote: Applicants must “match” with an advisor in order to be admitted to either program. | Only students who have successfully matched to a faculty advisor will be considered for admission.

funding.value: Students are typically supported through teaching and research assistantships providing a stipend and tuition waiver (faculty sponsor develops a multi-semester funding plan during application).
funding.quote: Graduate students in the Biology, Cellular and Molecular Biology programs are typically supported through a combination of teaching and research assistantships.

entry_route.value: Bachelor's degree in biology, chemistry, biochemistry, or a related discipline (3.0 overall and major GPA plus prior research experience required for Ph.D.).
entry_route.quote: Bachelor's degree in Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, or a related discipline | Students with a bachelor's degree may apply to either the M.S. or Ph.D. program; however, students with limited research experience should consider the M.S. program first.

notes: Interdisciplinary ~5-year Ph.D. in Biochemistry, Cell and Molecular Biology across the College of Science and Engineering and College of Medicine.
name: Ph.D. in Biochemistry, Cell and Molecular Biology
